article: Create a shortcut to lock a Windows computer
scope: Read the complete Japanese article and all twelve translations; checked shortcut/API behavior, Windows+L, session/security claims, images and alt/reference links, metadata, and the localized note on Japanese UI screenshots.
findings: Removed the duplicate future date (2026-09-24), restored the original publication date (2024-04-01), and set lastmod to the review date in all 13 editions.
Removed unrelated links to an RDBMS transaction-lock article from the Windows device-lock instructions.
Confirmed the shortcut target with Microsoft Learn and clarified that the Win32 function acts on an interactive signed-in session; locking does not sign out or directly close applications.
Retained Windows+L as the built-in alternative and documented that unlocking requires sign-in.
Added localized caveats that screenshots show Japanese Windows UI and menu labels can vary by version and display language; added Microsoft Support and Learn references.

terminology.note: Checked workstation lock, lock screen, shortcut target, Windows key+L, sign-in/unlock, interactive desktop, and rundll32 terminology across all editions.

mathematics.note: The article contains no mathematical claims or formulas.

code.note: Verified `rundll32.exe user32.dll,LockWorkStation` against Microsoft Learn PowerShell examples and checked that the LockWorkStation API is asynchronous and only works from an interactive desktop; reviewed the shortcut steps and Win+L key sequence.
